cat > /workspace/project/README.md <<'MD'
# H3Act offline evidence pipeline

Run `python3 -B main.py` with one UTF-8 JSON document on stdin. The command emits
one JSON result, or `{"error":"input"}` for an invalid document. It performs no
network I/O, real sleeps, subprocess creation, or runtime downloads. The target
runtime is CPython 3.11.14 with Pydantic 2.12.5.

## Components

* `main.py` handles strict JSON decoding, domain budgets, template coordinates,
  and orchestration. Duplicate object members and nonfinite JSON numbers fail.
* `schema.py` validates frame types without coercion and compiles templates into
  opaque byte sequences, preserving ordered and duplicate header pairs.
* `modules/byte_program.py` implements the restricted AST interpreter and shared
  byte ropes. Checksums compose algebraically; repeats and byte slices never
  require expanding large payloads. Only bounded capture ranges are decoded.
* `modules/fuzz_adapter.py` preserves compiled bytes, encodes exact receipts,
  and supplies the offline transport to `HTTP3_Just_Send.HttpClient`.
* `modules/clock.py` drives socket-free coroutines in the documented timestamp
  and priority order. The client retains early responses through send pauses,
  fixes terminal states, and enforces request-end/send-error behavior.
* `modules/capture_audit.py` frames independent HTTP/1.1 captures, summarizes
  opaque and deframed bodies, attributes raw spans, records per-part publication
  counts, and derives paired request/case diagnostics using actual identity
  bytes rather than checksum equality.

Run regression tests with `python3 -B -m unittest test_pipeline`. The external
public checker can be run with `python3 /workspace/check.py /workspace/project`.
The full behavioral and runtime contracts are in the provided `PROTOCOL.md` and
`RUNTIME.md` outside the submission tree.
MD
cd /workspace/project && python3 -B -m unittest test_pipeline && python3 -B main.py < /workspace/sample.json
python3 /workspace/check.py /workspace/project
find /workspace/project -type f -printf '%p %s bytes\n' | sort
